analysis.evidence: אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ identifies the speakers as addressing one another. Their words begin with הָבָה נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים, “Come, let us make bricks.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks the Qal wayyiqtol. The י־ prefix and ־וּ ending mark the third person masculine plural.

analysis.evidence: After the plural וַיֹּאמְרוּ ‘they said’, אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ means ‘each to his fellow’. אִישׁ singles out each speaker in the reciprocal exchange.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, used distributively.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ, “they said to one another,” אֶל introduces רֵעֵהוּ, the fellow whom each speaker addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.
